title: 19-20. AN OLD FATHER AND A YOUNG SON

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'My lord asked his servants, "Do you have a father or a brother?" And we answered, "We have an aged father, and there is a young son born to him in his old age. His brother is dead, and he is the only one of his mother's sons left, and his father loves him."'" — Gen 44:19-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Judah begins by talking about his father's love — and about the son who is loved.

Think about how much this must cost him. Jacob's favouritism was the wound that started everything. It was because their father loved Joseph more that the brothers hated him enough to sell him. And here is Judah, calmly telling a stranger, "his father loves him," without a trace of bitterness.

Something has died in Judah, and something better has grown in its place. He has stopped resenting his father's love for another son. He can now speak of it as simple fact rather than a grievance.

That is one of the surest signs of God's work in a heart: when the thing that used to make us bitter no longer does. Not because it never hurt, and not because it was fair, but because God has healed the place where the resentment lived.

Notice too the phrase "his brother is dead." Judah says it while standing in front of that very brother. What he mourns as lost is standing right in front of him, alive. God is often nearer to restoring what we have given up on than we can possibly imagine.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What old grievance is God inviting you to hand over to Him?
2. Is there something you have written off as dead that God may still restore?
3. Where has jealousy or comparison damaged a relationship in your life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, heal the places in me where old resentment still lives. Free me from comparison and jealousy, and give me a heart that can rejoice in the good You give to others. Amen.
